default: Variant A: land-tenure profile only. Variant B: A + village size + registration age.
reason: A keeps clusters interpretable as tenure types and keeps flood / RDTR / years / geography free to validate them. B is offered so the effect of extras can be measured.
evidence: distance rank correlation A versus B = 0.905; composition block alone versus A = 0.921

default: Not in A; log10 area in B.
alternatives_considered: include in both; exclude from both
reason: Area is extremely skewed and would dominate distances; tenure type should not just be village size.
evidence: B differs from A by rho = 0.905

default: Share of parcel AREA, not of parcel count.
reason: Area shows what the land is used for (HGU is 0.02% of parcels but about 17% of the area); counts mostly say how subdivided a village is, and parcel size / density already cover that.
evidence: distance rank correlation, count shares versus area shares = 0.621

default: Rights below 1% of total area are grouped into 'other': hak_pengelolaan, hak_wakaf, lainnya.
reason: Fewer, steadier parts; the rare ones are zero in almost every village. HGU is kept separate because it holds a large share of the area.
evidence: distance rank correlation, ungrouped versus grouped = 1.0: the geometry is unchanged

alternatives_considered: raw shares; centred log-ratio (CLR) with zero replacement
reason: Shares sum to 1, so raw distances are distorted; CLR cannot handle the many exact zeros without an arbitrary replacement value; sqrt tolerates zeros and needs no parameter.
evidence: raw shares rho = 0.945; CLR rho = 0.704 / 0.78 / 0.668 for replacement 1e-4 / 1e-3 / 1e-2; two CLR variants versus each other = 0.558

default: Dropped: titled share, coverage (log, clipped), count-based shares, per-right mean sizes.
reason: titled share = 1 - kosong share (max deviation 0e+00); log10 density + log10 mean parcel size = log10 coverage + 4 (max deviation 1e-15), so coverage adds no information and a third column would make the matrix rank-deficient.
Both are extremely right-skewed; the log removes the tail without needing a cap.
evidence: skew of mean parcel size 121.4 -> 1.33; parcel density 4.1 -> -0.97

default: Not fitted (1,950 analysis rows); listed in place_later.
reason: Shares are undefined (0/0); imputing would invent a tenure profile. They are a distinct, informative group.
evidence: see 4-5; 53% of them have zero flood area (all analysis rows: 22%) and 4% have an RDTR (all analysis rows: 17%)

default: Not fitted; listed in place_later with the reason.
reason: Placeholders and zero-area villages have no meaningful profile; for ratio outliers the area-based features are unreliable.
They look like ordinary, denser villages with overlapping parcels; dropping them biases the sample toward sparse villages.
evidence: dropping the overshoot rows changes median parcel density by -26.9% (Step 3b-9)

default: Robust z-score for the log / age columns; composition block scaled jointly to 5 units of variance (5 = parts - 1).
alternatives_considered: z-score every column; each concept counts once; no scaling
reason: Z-scoring every column would inflate the rare-right columns to the same weight as common ones; one unit per degree of freedom keeps the geometry honest.
evidence: z-score every column: rho 0.934 (composition = 75.0% of total variance (default 70.1%)); each concept counts once (composition = 1): rho 0.894 (composition = 31.9% of total variance (default 70.1%)); composition and log block equal: rho 0.971 (composition = 50.0% of total variance (default 70.1%)); no scaling: rho 0.762 (composition = 15.7% of total variance (default 70.1%))

default: Interpretation only; never used to build clusters.
reason: Zero flood area is ambiguous and strongly regional; RDTR exists for ~17% of villages; years are undefined for untitled villages; geography should be an outcome, not an input.
Each flag is already visible in the matching share (a zero share = flag false).

default: log(1 + years since the median registration year).
reason: Raw age has a long right tail (up to 60+ years) that would dominate distances for a few percent of villages.
